hints.title: Two-Color Partition Obstacle
hints.text: Partitioning graph vertices into two independent sets such that every edge connects different sets requires detecting odd cycles. How can alternating two colors across adjacent vertices verify bipartiteness?

hints.title: Bicolor Alternation Invariant
hints.text: In a bipartite graph, if vertex u is colored 1, all of its neighbors v must be colored -1. Finding a neighbor with color identical to u proves an odd cycle exists.

hints.title: Multi-Component Coloring Procedure
hints.text: Allocate color array of size n with 0 (unvisited). Iterate i from 0 to n - 1: if color[i] == 0, color it 1 and enqueue i. Pop u; for each neighbor v of u: if color[v] == 0, color it -color[u] and enqueue v. If color[v] == color[u], return false. If all components color cleanly, return true.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Every vertex and edge is examined at most once during two-color traversal.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all subsets of vertices takes O(2^V) exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Color array and queue take O(V) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling disconnected components by looping through all vertices 0 to n - 1.
